subject: DPA: processor list change & objection timeline — signing milestones
messages:
From: Erin Shaw <erin.shaw@acmecorp.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Doug Miller <dmiller@cloudbroker.com>, AcmeCorp Legal <legal@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-31T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed processor addition + timing question

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for taking time on the call this morning. Per our procurement checklist, AcmeCorp is planning to add CloudBroker as a permitted subprocessor for telemetry forwarding (event delivery only). We attached our proposed processor description and would like to understand Redwood's notification and objection window for this category of change.

Two short questions:
- Can Redwood accept a 30-day notification window for this type of telemetry-only addition?
- If we proceed, will you require a new DocuSign envelope for the updated DPA or can this be handled via an addendum?

If helpful, I can loop in our security contact to confirm the narrow scope. We are aiming to finish procurement and signatures before our internal onboarding on 2026-11-20.

Best,
Erin Shaw
Head of Platform Security — AcmeCorp
[Attachment: Updated Processor List v3.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Erin Shaw <erin.shaw@acmecorp.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.inference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-31T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed processor addition + timing question

Erin —

Appreciate the doc and the clear scope. Short answers up front:
- Our standard DPA language uses a 45-day notification window for new subprocessors, primarily to give enterprise customers time to review, object, and for us to handle any contractual redlines.
- That said, for telemetry-forwarding-only processors (no persistent customer data retention beyond routing), we have some flexibility and have agreed to 30 days on a case-by-case basis when there is a strong business justification.

Two proposed next steps:
1) We will run the Updated Processor List through Privacy to confirm the narrow scope. Neha, can you confirm the telemetry-only classification and whether there are any additional controls we should call out?
2) If Privacy signs off, we can prepare a short addendum (one-page) that references the current DPA and the new processor. We typically execute via DocuSign (single envelope) unless legal redlines require a full DPA re-execution.

Erin, if you can confirm AcmeCorp's tolerance for an addendum vs full re-sign, we will expedite. Goal: get an addendum prepared by 2026-11-05 to meet your onboarding date.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — redwood.inference.com
[DocuSign draft will link here once prepared]

On Sun, Oct 31, 2026 at 13:22 PST, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Karthik / Erin —
>
> I reviewed the Updated Processor List. CloudBroker only receives streaming telemetry (event payloads) and does not persist PII beyond short-term buffering in their ingestion pipeline. From a controls perspective we should require:
> - Contractual prohibition on downstream resale of event payloads
> - Retention maximum of 7 days (unless otherwise agreed)
> - Access controls / least-privilege for the service account
> If those are added to the addendum we can treat this as telemetry-only and I'm comfortable with a 30-day notification window for this specific case.
>
> Priyom — can we prepare a draft addendum and mark those three controls as required clauses?
>
> Neha Kapoor
> Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
> [Attachment: DPA_redlines_ERIN_2026.docx (docx)]

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.inference.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com>, Erin Shaw <erin.shaw@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed processor addition + timing question

Team —

Thanks — attaching the draft 1-page addendum and a checklist of execution steps. Summary:
- Addendum includes the three required controls (no resale, 7-day retention, role-based access).
- We will reference the existing DPA, append the Updated Processor List v3.xlsx, and include an explicit effective date clause.
- Execution plan: prepare DocuSign envelope -> internal Legal & Privacy countersign -> send to AcmeCorp legal for signature.

Timeline I recommend:
- 2026-11-03: finalize addendum text (internal review)
- 2026-11-04: send DocuSign to AcmeCorp for signature (30-day notice window begins on send date)
- 2026-11-10: expected counter-signature if no objection raised

Erin — can you confirm that AcmeCorp will accept an addendum executed via DocuSign envelope (link will be provided) and that the 30-day countdown from send date is acceptable? If you want a longer notice running from the announcement to end users, say so and we can adjust language.

Attachments: DocuSign_Envelope_98765.pdf (placeholder for envelope once created)

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Legal Operations — Redwood Inference
